title: A/B tests and iteration
task_statement: Compare a change against a control with one primary metric before you ship it. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: A/B test design
components.first_principle: A control arm shows whether the change, and not the traffic mix, caused the measured difference.

nodes.label: Arm A: current prompt or model
Arm B: candidate prompt or model

steps: Write the hypothesis and the primary metric before the test starts.
Assign each user or ticket to one arm and keep that assignment.
Set the sample size before launch for the lift that you need to detect. (Inference)
Run both arms over the same period and the same traffic mix.
Compare the primary metric for each arm with the threshold in the hypothesis.
Choose ship, roll back, or iterate before you read the result. (Inference)
pros: A control arm separates the effect of the change from traffic changes. (Inference)
The test uses the same primary metric as the offline evaluation.
The docs list A/B testing as a method to compare against a baseline or earlier version.
cons: The test needs enough traffic for the lift size that you claim. (Inference)
Users in the candidate arm see its answers, and any defects in them. (Inference)
A test with two changes at once cannot show which change caused the result. (Inference)
use_when: A prompt, model, or tool change can move the primary metric.
A team needs a ship decision that rests on a measured comparison.
The comparison unit is a ticket or a user, and each unit keeps one arm.
do_not_use_when: Traffic is too low to reach the planned sample size. (Inference)
The change carries a safety risk and the arm would expose users to it. (Inference)
The team has no primary metric yet, so no arm can win or lose. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Log which arm served each request. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Keep the assignment rule in version control. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Compare the arms on cost per completed task.
constraints.combination: Add the spend per arm to the report. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track cache read and write token counts for each arm.
constraints.combination: Expect cache misses when the arms use different models.

constraints.choice: Record latency per arm for the guard metric. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D4.3. Expect a scenario where a team ships a change with no control and sees a small score move. The credited answer sets a control arm, a hypothesis, and a primary metric first. (Inference)
components.trap: A full rollout that compares the week before with the week after. The traffic mix changed, so the difference does not show the effect of the change.
components.decision_rule: Assign each unit to one arm, and compare the arms on the primary metric with a stated threshold.
components.exam_tip: A significant result that fails the business value check does not justify the switch. (Inference)

key_facts.text: The docs list A/B testing as a method to compare performance against a baseline model or earlier version.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs describe a held-out test set as the basis for a success criterion.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The model_changed cache miss type applies when a router, A/B test, or fallback selects a different model.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The cache is per model, so each model keeps a separate prompt cache.
key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: Iteration by model and effort
components.first_principle: A newer model or higher effort earns its extra cost only when it completes more tasks.

nodes.label: Failed tasks re-run at higher effort

steps: Run the baseline and the candidate on the same eval set.
Check the quality floor and the guard metrics before you compare cost.
Compare cost per completed task, not cost per token.
Re-run only the failed tasks at a higher effort when outcomes are checkable.
Audit the prompts against the model after each model change.
pros: Cost per completed task compares models on the same unit of value.
The docs report that failure-only re-runs at higher effort cost less than a fixed high effort in Anthropic measurements.
A model change can be tested on traffic without a full rollout. (Inference)
cons: Re-runs add latency for the tasks that fail the first pass. (Inference)
Anthropic measurements use benchmarks that may not match your tasks. (Inference)
Prompts written for an older model can add cost on a newer model.
use_when: Budget binds and the outcome of each task can be checked.
The team considers a newer model for the same workload.
Effort settings differ in cost and quality, and the floor is known.
do_not_use_when: The outcome of a task cannot be checked by code or a grader. (Inference)
The latency limit leaves no room for a second pass. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Compare candidates on cost per completed task.
constraints.combination: Add the re-run share to the cost report. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Re-run only failed tasks to limit the extra latency.
constraints.combination: Use a higher effort only on the tasks that need it. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Audit prompts against the current model after each model change.
Route only the failed tasks to the higher effort tier.

components.exam_tie: D4.3. Expect a scenario where a team wants to change the model after a test. The credited answer compares cost per completed task and checks the quality floor first. (Inference)
components.trap: A switch to a larger model because its score is higher. The score rises, but the cost per completed task may rise faster than the gain.
components.decision_rule: Ship a model or effort change only when it clears the quality floor and lowers or holds cost per completed task.
components.exam_tip: A higher per-token price does not decide the switch. Compare the completed-task cost instead.

key_facts.text: The docs say to compare models on cost per completed task, not per token.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs call a low-effort first pass, with failed tasks re-run at a higher effort, the cheapest policy in Anthropic measurements.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs say to audit prompts against the current model, and again whenever the model changes.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The docs say each newer model solved at least as many tasks as the one before, in Anthropic measurements.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: In Anthropic tests, low effort with failures re-run at high cost about 40% less than all tasks at high, at the same pass rate.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 default to medium effort. Other models that support effort default to high.
key_facts.label: Fact

not_in_source: A general claim that newer models always cost less per task. Not in source.
The effort level that fits a given workload. Not in source.

flowchart LR
  H[Hypothesis] --> P[Primary metric]
  P --> A[Arm A control]
  P --> B[Arm B candidate]
  A --> R[Compare on threshold]
  B --> R
  R --> C[Cost per completed task]
  R --> K[Keep arm assignment fixed]
  K --> M[Cache is per model]

patterns.wording: a full rollout shows a small score move with no control
patterns.answer_type: A/B test with a control arm
patterns.rule: Assign units to a control and a candidate arm, and compare one primary metric.
traps: Ship and watch the next week

patterns.wording: the test shows a real lift that costs more than it returns
patterns.rule: Separate statistical significance from business value. Decide with the cost of the switch.
traps: Ship because the lift is significant
Run the test longer to find a bigger lift

patterns.wording: a candidate change touches tools or permissions
patterns.rule: Measure the candidate on logged or copied traffic before users see it. (Inference)
